title: The image of the fundamental group of a connected finite etale cover
statement: Let $f:Y'\to Y$ be a finite etale morphism of connected schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\bar y'$ a geometric point of $Y'$ and $\bar y=f\circ\bar y'$. Regard $Y'$, with $f$, as an object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ [def-galois-categories]; then $\bar y'$ is an element of $|Y'_{\bar y}|$. Let $f_*:\pi_1(Y',\bar y')\to\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ be the continuous homomorphism of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and $U\subset\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ the stabilizer of $\bar y'$ for the action of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ on $|Y'_{\bar y}|$ of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Then the image of $f_*$ is $U$, and $U$ is an open subgroup of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ of index $\#|Y'_{\bar y}|$.

source.place: SGA 1 V, Proposition 6.13 ('u : pi_F' -> pi_F est un isomorphisme de pi_F' sur le sous-groupe ouvert U de pi_F stabilisateur de l'element marque a'; 'La demonstration est laissee au lecteur') and §7, p. 116, last paragraph (the case of an etale cover S' of S)

proof.text: Write $G=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$, $G'=\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$, $P=(Y'\xrightarrow{f}Y)$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, and $a=\bar y'\in|P_{\bar y}|$. By [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], $f_*$ is characterized by $f_*(h)\cdot\tau_R(z)=\tau_R(h\cdot z)$ for every finite etale $R/Y$ and $z\in|(R\times_YY')_{\bar y'}|$. For $R=P$, the diagonal $d:Y'\to Y'\times_YY'$ is a section of the second projection, and its value $d(\bar y')$ maps under $\tau_P$ to $a$. Every $h\in G'$ fixes $d(\bar y')$: $d$ is a morphism from the final object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$, whose fibre has one element, and the components of a natural automorphism commute with its fibre map. Hence $f_*(h)\cdot a=a$, so $\operatorname{im}(f_*)\subseteq U$.

source.place: SGA 1, Expose V, Proposition 6.13, pp. 114-115, inclusion of the induced group in the stabilizer; proof omitted there

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion let $g\in U$. Take any $Q=(Z\xrightarrow{q}Y')$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$. The composite $f\circ q:Z\to Y$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), so it is an object $\widetilde Q$ of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$. The fibre $|Q_{\bar y'}|$ identifies with the subset $T_Q=\{z\in|\widetilde Q_{\bar y}|:q(z)=a\}$: a point over $\bar y'$ is exactly a geometric point of $Z$ over $\bar y$ whose composite with $q$ is the specified point $a$ of $Y'$. Since $q:\widetilde Q\to P$ is a morphism in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, naturality of the $G$-action gives $q(g\cdot z)=g\cdot q(z)=g\cdot a=a$ for $z\in T_Q$; thus $g$ preserves $T_Q$. The same holds for $g^{-1}$ because it also fixes $a$, so the restriction is a bijection of $|Q_{\bar y'}|$.

source.place: SGA 1, Expose V, Proposition 6.13, pp. 114-115: objects over the connected object $S$ and the fibre as inverse image of the marked element; proof omitted there

proof.text: If $u:Q\to Q'$ is a morphism over $Y'$, it is also a morphism $\widetilde Q\to\widetilde Q'$ over $Y$, so $u(g\cdot z)=g\cdot u(z)$; the restrictions of step 2 therefore form a natural automorphism of the fibre functor on $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$, with inverse obtained from $g^{-1}$. Through the equivalence with $\mathrm{FLC}(Y')$ compatible with fibres [thm-galois-lc-etale], this is an element $h\in G'$ as defined in [def-galois-fibre-functor]. For any $R\in\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, put $Q=R\times_YY'$; the projection $Q\to R$ is a morphism over $Y$ and restricts on $T_Q$ to the bijection $\tau_R$ of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Therefore $\tau_R(h\cdot z)=g\cdot\tau_R(z)$ for every $z\in|Q_{\bar y'}|$. The defining characterization of $f_*$ in that lemma, and faithfulness of evaluation in [def-galois-fibre-functor], imply $f_*(h)=g$. Thus $U\subseteq\operatorname{im}(f_*)$.

source.place: SGA 1, Expose V, Proposition 6.13, pp. 114-115, reverse inclusion in the asserted isomorphism; proof omitted there

proof.text: The subgroup $U$ is open: by [def-galois-fibre-functor] evaluation $G\to\operatorname{Aut}(|P_{\bar y}|)$ is continuous for the discrete topology on the finite permutation group, and $U$ is the inverse image of the point stabilizer of $a$. Since $Y'$ is connected, [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object] makes $P$ a connected object of the Galois category $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ [lem-fet-galois-category]; [lem-galois-transitive] says that $G$ acts transitively on $|P_{\bar y}|$. The map $G/U\to|P_{\bar y}|$, $gU\mapsto g\cdot a$, is well defined since elements of $U$ fix $a$, injective since $g_1\cdot a=g_2\cdot a$ iff $g_2^{-1}g_1\in U$, and surjective by transitivity. Hence the index $[G:U]$ is $\#|Y'_{\bar y}|$, including the one-point case.

split_report.summary: SGA 1 V.6.13 states this result but leaves the proof to the reader. The split gives both inclusions explicitly by functoriality and restriction of natural automorphisms to the marked fibre, then derives openness from the evaluation topology and index from transitivity. Existing nodes cover composition of finite and etale maps. The connected-object step has a new node with an exact sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration reported for lead attachment. No exact sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration was found for the item itself.
split_report.blueprint: The four steps realize the final sentence of thm-galois-fundamental's blueprint proof: 'the limit of the corresponding automorphism groups is the stabilizer of the fibre ... an open subgroup because stabilizers in a finite continuous pi_1-set are open'; steps 1-3 establish the stabilizer identity, and step 4 its openness and index.

lean.statement: theorem fundamentalGroupMap_range_eq_stabilizer {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X] [ConnectedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] [Etale f] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (GX GY : Type u) [Group GX] [TopologicalSpace GX] [IsTopologicalGroup GX] [CompactSpace GX] [∀ Q, MulAction GX ((fiber s).obj Q)] [IsFundamentalGroup (fiber s) GX] [Group GY] [TopologicalSpace GY] [IsTopologicalGroup GY] [CompactSpace GY] [∀ P, MulAction GY ((fiber (s ≫ f)).obj P)] [IsFundamentalGroup (fiber (s ≫ f)) GY] : let P : Y.FiniteEtale := ⟨Etale.mk f, inferInstanceAs (IsFinite f)⟩ let a : (fiber (s ≫ f)).obj P := fiberMk (s ≫ f) P s rfl let U := MulAction.stabilizer GY a (fundamentalGroupMap (pullbackFiberIso f s) GX GY).range = U ∧ IsOpen (U : Set GY) ∧ U.index = Nat.card ((fiber (s ≫ f)).obj P)
lean.note: Uses the recorded finite-etale fibre functor and functorial fundamentalGroupMap. GX and GY are arbitrary compact fundamental-group models as in the source library; toAutContinuousMulEquiv identifies them with the automorphism groups. The finite-etale and FLC fibre descriptions correspond under thm-galois-lc-etale, already referenced in the node.

reviewed_lean.note: connected X,Y (ConnectedSpace); f IsFinite+Etale; s : Spec Ω ⟶ X, Ω IsAlgClosed, ybar = s≫f; P = ⟨Etale.mk f,_⟩ has obj.left = X, obj.hom = f (rfl); a = fiberMk s; f_* = recorded fundamentalGroupMap (pullbackFiberIso f s = pr1∘z); π1 as IsFundamentalGroup models in u (forced by fundamentalGroupMap, ≅ Aut F via toAutContinuousMulEquiv); U = MulAction.stabilizer; range = U ∧ IsOpen U ∧ U.index = Nat.card fibre
